events.label: Starting conditions: default seed 24369; entering turn 4 of stage2-victory.txt. Customer #1 was served on turn 3 and occupies Table 1; Table 2 is free. VIP #2 has not arrived yet. r = restaurant; results are returned as ActionResult / GameView.

Successful ActionResult returns through Waiter / StaffTeam / GameController; Waiter lastActionTurn=4 and phase=AWAIT_CHEF. CLI selects Chef WAIT through submitChefAction -> StaffTeam.executeChef -> Chef.execute; phase becomes AUTO. Queue/table mutation occurs inside SeatingArea.seat().

VIP satisfaction becomes 95. Customer #1 becomes READY_TO_PAY on turn 4 but cannot pay until turn 5. The same finishTurn ordering is used on every turn: eating -> Cashier -> penalty -> completeTurn -> result evaluation.
TURN 5 - manager choice and actual VIP order
[manager takes VIP order now; main branch follows the recorded victory priority rule]

OrderPort.Factory.create(2,vip,Burger,1350) is bound to Order::new. Restaurant validates the fresh order, stores it, and returns success. The bill is final on the Order. Successful Waiter execution records its allowance; controller phase becomes AWAIT_CHEF. Invalid input/action would retry without advancing phase or using allowance.
Order 2 becomes READY with preparedUnits=1 and readyTurn=5. The Waiter has already acted and cannot serve again this turn. Chef success returns through StaffTeam; phase becomes AUTO.

Automatic Cashier chain as on turn 4: customer #1 is now eligible and pays $9.00; Table 1 is released. Those Order 1 / Customer 1 messages are outside this VIP lifeline and are intentionally collapsed here.
completeTurn(5); GameResult.evaluate(summary5) returns IN_PROGRESS. The order being READY does not stop waiting loss: VIP is still ORDERED until served.
TURN 6 - serve the dish on a later turn
Waiter success; Chef WAIT; CLI calls finishTurn(). Staff capacity is still one task / preparation unit per turn.
Cashier finds no eligible VIP. Waiting penalty leaves a SERVED customer unchanged; completeTurn(6) and result evaluation follow. VIP satisfaction stays 90.
TURN 7 - one full turn of eating; no immediate payment
startTurn() on turn 7 also creates Regular customer #3. From the recorded policy: Waiter seats #3; Chef waits. Those non-VIP messages are collapsed. CLI then calls finishTurn().
Penalty applies only to unserved customers: VIP remains at 90. completeTurn(7); evaluate -> IN_PROGRESS.
TURN 8 - automatic payment, snapshot and table release
startTurn() on turn 8; recorded staff choices take Regular #3 order and prepare its first Pasta unit. CLI then calls finishTurn().
SeatingArea calls Table 2.release(). Order 2 retains billCents=1350, paidTurn=8 and satisfactionAtPayment=90. Revenue is computed from PAID orders; unpaid/abandoned orders are excluded.
TURNS 9-18 - complete the game; same victory/defeat criteria

For every turn: arrivals on 10/13/16; one Waiter choice, then one Chef choice; advanceEating -> automatic oldest payment -> per-customer penalty / abandonment -> completeTurn. All other-customer interactions follow stage2-victory.txt.

TAKE_ORDER branch final outcome: 18/18 turns; 5 paid; $64.50; average paid satisfaction 80.40; zero unhappy departures. CLI prints the final result. Critic #6 cannot pay before the deadline, as intended.
[manager chooses WAIT on turn 5; same priority rule resumes on turn 6]

Separate counterfactual replay: VIP orders/prepares on turn 6, is served on turn 7, becomes READY_TO_PAY on turn 8 and pays on turn 9. Its payment snapshot is 85. The remaining customers are also scheduled by the same priority rule. Final result: VICTORY, 5 paid, $64.50, satisfaction sum 389, average 77.80. Thus one staff-priority choice changes timing and satisfaction, while both runs still win.
